findings.issue: The effective catalog is still not guaranteed to be the one the gate evaluates. Line 100 exempts the catalog from the offset check, but nothing requires the final xref entry for the catalog to point past revisionEnd. When that entry keeps the signed offset, line 104 skips the catalog, so the effective catalog is never compared with `complete.catalog`. Separately, the header regex on line 118 (`(^|[^0-9A-Za-z])(\d+)\s+(\d+)\s+obj\b`) is narrower than pdf-lib's linear parser, which accepts `endobj1 0 obj` (after `endobj`, the loop in PDFParser.parseIndirectObjects continues on any digit) and `1%c\n0%c\nobj` (via skipWhitespaceAndComments). I ran a counterexample in memory by calling `readPdfTrustEvidence` directly under node --experimental-strip-types, writing no files. It kept the signed revision of `pades-blt.pdf`, appended objects 8–14 and then `...endobj1 0 obj << /Type /Catalog ... /DSS 8 0 R >>` glued on with no delimiter, and omitted object 1 from the new xref. The function returned certs=2, ocsp=2, crls=1, and pdf-lib reports a catalog with /DSS. An xref reader (pdf.js/Acrobat), however, resolves 1 0 R to the original catalog, which has no DSS. So a shadow catalog passes, and the proof can claim PAdES-B-LT/DSS evidence that does not exist in the effective document. Signed content is not changed, because original objects keep their offsets and are compared with the pdf-lib view. The false B-LT claim, though, violates the ciclo 3 decision (fail closed when effective semantics are not established) and the requirement that the catalog be compared with the effective object.
findings.required_change: Require `final.entries.get(catalogNumber)` to be in use with offset >= revisionEnd, so the catalog must be updated by the DSS revision. This sends it down the parse-at-offset path and the structural comparison with `context.lookup(catalogRef)`, and it must also equal `complete.catalog`. Stop using the header regex as the census of appended objects. Instead, make pdf-lib's view match the xref: every ref in `complete.context` whose object comes from the suffix must have a final xref entry whose parse at its offset equals it. Alternatively, fail closed on any `obj` token in the suffix that lies outside the intervals, including headers without a preceding delimiter or separated by comments. The Inspector adds negatives for a catalog that is not updated in the xref with a glued `endobj1 0 obj`, and for a comment-separated header `1%\n0%\nobj`, both expecting 'Post-signature modification'.

findings.issue: Fixture gap. `appendCatalogShadow` covers only a catalog repointed into a stream body, where parse at the offset and pdf-lib differ. There is no negative for a catalog that keeps the signed offset while pdf-lib picks up a DSS catalog through a header outside the regex. The four required negatives (catalog shadow after a fake endstream, hybrid XRefStm type 1/2, duplicate /Prev) exist in `trust-gate.spec.ts:510-519` and would be rejected by lines 66-67, 70-74 and 111 of the source. I did not run the tests.
findings.required_change: Add the negative described in the blocking finding next to `appendCatalogShadow`, asserting the exact message 'Post-signature modification'.

findings.issue: TSA anchors are now intersected with `profile.trustAnchorsPem` (line 247), which resolves the ciclo 4 policy. The TSA chain, however, is still validated with `checkDate: now` rather than genTime. An old document whose TSA certificate later expires stops verifying, even with valid post-TST evidence. The fixtures still use a two-level PKI (root→signer/TSA) with the root as OCSP responder, so there is no sensor for an intermediate, a revoked intermediate, or a delegated responder without id-kp-OCSPSigning.
findings.required_change: Validate the TSA chain at `tst.genTime`, or document the choice in the contract. Generate a root→intermediate→signer/TSA PKI and the corresponding negatives (fixture gap).

findings.issue: A PDF that uses only xref streams, or with /XRefStm in the signed trailer, fails as 'Post-signature modification' (SignatureTrustError → invalid/tampered). Unsupported format is indeterminacy, not proof of modification. It stays fail-closed, so it is not blocking.
findings.required_change: Emit a distinct error for an unsupported xref format (e.g. SignatureTrustUnavailableError or an 'unsupported xref' reason) and keep 'Post-signature modification' for actual divergence.

findings.issue: Revocation after TST is now correct: the revoked CRL/OCSP are generated after the TST, and `trust-gate.spec.ts:639-653` asserts `SignatureTrustError`/'Certificate revoked'. The pre-TST→fresh fallback is covered by `pades-stale-ocsp-fresh-crl`, which yields B-LT via CRL. Two fixture gaps remain. There is no single fixture with pre-TST 'good' evidence plus post-TST revoked evidence in the same DSS; the pre-TST case is proven only in isolation. There is also no stale-OCSP→fresh-OCSP fallback under an OCSP-only profile.
findings.required_change: Add a fixture whose DSS carries both a pre-TST good OCSP and a post-TST revoked CRL/OCSP, expecting 'Certificate revoked'. Add the OCSP-only fallback case.

summary: FAIL. I reviewed the code read-only and did not run the test suite. The one exception was an in-memory run of `readPdfTrustEvidence` (node strip-types, no file writes) to confirm the counterexample. Resolved in ciclo 5: each appended xref target is parsed at its real offset with the pdf-lib parser, and /Length must equal the content size. The object at that offset is compared structurally with `context.lookup`, so a catalog repointed into a stream now fails. Object intervals may not overlap. The trailer is parsed as a real dictionary, with duplicate keys and /XRefStm rejected and non-'xref' sections failing closed. /Prev of the first appended section must equal the signed startxref, and /Root, /Encrypt and /Info are preserved. The required negatives exist: catalog shadow after a fake endstream, hybrid type 1 and 2, and duplicate /Prev. CRL/OCSP revoked after the TST are asserted with 'Certificate revoked'. The old→fresh evidence fallback continues iterating and has a fixture. TSA anchors are intersected with the profile. `verify` maps SignatureProviderResponseError and SignatureEvidenceMismatchError (synthetic evidence) to `invalid`. The withdrawal binding through the catalog of the signed prefix follows the Architect amendment: the source is the exact prefix before ByteRange[1], and the certificate comes from the tenant port. One blocking defect remains. The catalog entry in the final xref may keep the signed offset (line 100 exemption plus the skip on line 104). Meanwhile the header regex on line 118 misses `endobj1 0 obj` and comment-separated headers that pdf-lib accepts. I confirmed an in-memory counterexample: pdf-lib sees a catalog with /DSS, the effective xref points to the original catalog without DSS, and the gate accepts it. That produces a false B-LT claim, though it does not change signed content. Fixture gaps, listed separately: the negative for the non-updated catalog, a 3-level PKI and delegated responder, and pre-TST good plus post-TST revoked evidence in the same DSS. This FAIL does not release the SIG commit. Conformance and publication are out of scope.
